blocks.text: Transition metals, found in the d and f blocks of the Periodic Table, are known for their high density, good conductivity and coloured compounds. Iron has been the backbone of industry, from tools to modern steel; copper, silver and gold have long been used for coins and jewellery and are now essential in electronics and dentistry because they resist corrosion and conduct well. Transition metals are classed by where their outermost electrons are being filled: d-block (d orbitals) or f-block (f orbitals). This chapter studies the first row of the d block, the 3d series.

blocks.title: Transition element
blocks.text: A transition element is a d-block element that forms one or more stable ions with an incomplete (partly filled) d subshell.

The d block runs from Group 3 to Group 12, but in the first row scandium and zinc are not counted as transition elements. Zinc forms only one ion, Zn2+, whose 3d subshell is full: [Ar] 3d10 4s0. Scandium forms only Sc3+, whose 3d subshell is empty: [Ar] 3d0 4s0. Neither has a stable ion with a partly filled d subshell, so the first-row transition elements are titanium to copper.

blocks.prompt: Why is zinc a d-block element but not a transition element?
blocks.explanation: Its only ion, Zn2+, has a full 3d subshell ([Ar] 3d10), so it has no stable ion with an incomplete d subshell.

items: Transition element: d-block element with a stable ion having an incomplete d subshell.
First row: Ti to Cu; Sc (Sc3+, 3d0) and Zn (Zn2+, 3d10) are excluded.
